findings.description: The Vite ready regex `^\s*Local:\s+(\S+)` will NOT match real Vite output. Vite v8 banner prints `  ➜  Local:   http://127.0.0.1:5173/` with an arrow prefix character. The proposed predicate would never fire and `overview.dev_server.start` would time out while the server is actually running. The plan's Risk #4 includes a more permissive variant in a regex comment, but the Approach section's canonical regex is the strict one — these contradict each other and the canonical one is wrong.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a single canonical predicate that strips ANSI/control prefixes and then matches `Local:\s+(\S+)` anywhere in the line (not anchored to start). Pseudo: `const stripped = line.replace(/\x1b\[[0-9;]*[A-Za-z]/g, ''); const m = stripped.match(/Local:\s+(https?:\S+)/); if (m) return m[1];`. Document the canonical regex in the Approach section and update tests to assert both arrow-prefixed and plain variants are matched.
findings.resolution: Updated the plan to use one canonical Vite ready parser that strips ANSI escapes and matches Local URLs anywhere in the line, with tests for arrow-prefixed and plain banners.

findings.description: Double-start race is internally inconsistent. ProcessManager.spawn registers a `'starting'` record BEFORE the child emits the `'spawn'` event. During that window, a second call to `dev_server.start` throws `AlreadyRunning` and the tool layer is specified to return `{ alreadyRunning: true, url, pid, startedAt }` — but `url`, `pid`, and `startedAt` are undefined on the existing handle until the spawn event fires. The tool would return an object missing required fields.
findings.suggestedFix: When `AlreadyRunning` is caught, the tool should `await existing.readyPromise` (a Promise<{url, pid, startedAt}> that the manager exposes per handle). The promise resolves when the first caller's onReady completes. Both callers then return identical `{ ok: true, alreadyRunning: true, url, pid, startedAt }` after readiness. Plan must add `readyPromise` to the ManagedProcess type and document the await behavior in the tool's contract.
findings.resolution: Added readyPromise handling to the ProcessManager and dev_server.start plan so duplicate starts during the starting window wait for defined url, pid, and startedAt fields.

findings.description: The plan modifies `scripts/lib/sync-lock.mjs` to export `readLockStatus(lockPath)` but does NOT mention updating `scripts/lib/sync-lock.d.mts`. The `tools/overview-mcp` package is TypeScript with `NodeNext` resolution and imports `.mjs` modules through their `.d.mts` declaration files. Without adding the `readLockStatus` export to the type declarations, `pnpm --filter @codexu/overview-mcp typecheck` will fail and `sync-watch-status.ts` won't be able to import the helper.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `scripts/lib/sync-lock.d.mts` to the 'To modify' section. Declare `export function readLockStatus(lockPath: string, opts?: { staleAfterMs?: number }): Promise<{ state: 'missing' } | { state: 'active' | 'stale', pid: number, process: string, startedAt: string, mtime: Date }>;` plus any helper-export types if `parseLockMetadata` / `isLiveProcess` are factored out.
findings.resolution: Added the missing sync-lock declaration file update to the plan with the readLockStatus export signature.

findings.description: One-shot `overview.build` and `overview.sync.now` children are explicitly NOT tracked in `ProcessManager.Map`. This means `stopAll()` will not kill them. If SIGTERM arrives mid-build or mid-sync, those child processes are orphaned — directly violating the plan's own lifecycle constraint (acceptance criterion: 'When the MCP server receives SIGTERM/SIGINT, all spawned children are killed').
findings.suggestedFix: Track transient one-shots inside ProcessManager with reserved single-flight names ('build', 'sync-now'). Exclude them from `dev_server.status` reads (those tools only inspect 'dev-server'), but include them in `stopAll()` so SIGTERM cleans them up. The single-flight rejection (currently a module-level `isBuilding` boolean for build) becomes a property of the manager's `spawn()` method via the `AlreadyRunning` exception.
findings.resolution: Updated the plan so one-shot build and sync children are tracked by ProcessManager while running and are killed by stopAll during MCP shutdown.

findings.description: The planned summary line `sync: matched=${matched}, unmatched=${unmatched}, duration=${...}ms` uses identifiers `matched` and `unmatched` that do not exist as bindings in `scripts/sync-ralph-state.mjs:runOneShot()`. The plan must specify the exact derivation from the actual local state.
findings.suggestedFix: Specify exact derivation: `const matched = Object.keys(state.byTaskId ?? {}).length; const unmatched = (state.unmatched ?? []).length; const durationMs = Date.now() - startTime;` (where `startTime = Date.now()` is captured at the top of runOneShot). Verify the variable names against the actual runOneShot scope in the plan text — DO NOT assume; read the function and bind the names that exist.
findings.resolution: Updated the sync summary plan step to bind startTime and derive matched/unmatched counts from the actual runOneShot state object before logging.

findings.description: Extending `ServerContext` with a `processManager` field will break existing context construction sites, especially `tools/overview-mcp/src/__tests__/helpers.ts`. `makeContext()` currently returns the 3-field shape `{ repoRoot, config, snapshotReader }`. Adding a new required field will fail typecheck across all existing tests and tools unless every constructor and every fixture is updated atomically.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `tools/overview-mcp/src/__tests__/helpers.ts` to the 'To modify' file list. Specify that `makeContext()` (or whatever helper builds a test ServerContext) must construct a `ProcessManager` instance — or accept one as an optional override defaulting to a stub. Walk all ServerContext literals after the change and update them.
findings.resolution: Added the test helper and ServerContext literal audit/update requirement to the implementation strategy, file list, and US-004 story.

findings.description: Start-failure cleanup is missing. If `onReady` times out or the child exits before matching, `dev-server-start.ts` does not stop or remove the registered `'dev-server'` handle from `ProcessManager.Map`. A failed start leaves a stale `'starting'`-or-`'exited'` record that may block subsequent start attempts depending on how the AlreadyRunning check is implemented.
findings.suggestedFix: In `dev-server-start.ts`, wrap the spawn + onReady in try/catch. On any failure (timeout, exit-before-ready, error event), call `manager.stop('dev-server')` to remove the stale handle, then return `{ ok: false, error: <descriptive>, lastLogLines: stderr.slice(-30) }`. Add an acceptance criterion that covers the failed-start-then-retry path (second call to start must succeed if the first timed out).
findings.resolution: Added plan requirements for dev_server.start to clean up and remove stale process handles on startup failure, plus tests and acceptance coverage for retry-after-failure.

findings.description: Windows process model is under-specified. With `spawn('pnpm', args, { shell: true })`, the stored `pid` may be the shell wrapper (cmd.exe / pwsh.exe), not the Vite/Node process. Killing only that PID will not reliably satisfy the no-orphan acceptance criterion. The plan defers `tree-kill` as out of scope but this conflicts with the no-orphan AC.
findings.suggestedFix: EITHER (a) include `tree-kill` in v1 dependencies and use it inside ProcessManager.stop() on Windows (recommended — removes the AC ambiguity), OR (b) explicitly downgrade the no-orphan AC to 'best effort on Windows; verified for Vite specifically' and document the limitation in README. Pick one and commit. Do not leave the conflict open.
findings.resolution: Amended the plan to add tree-kill as a v1 dependency, require Windows process-tree termination in ProcessManager.stop(), and verify descendant PIDs in no-orphan acceptance tests.

findings.description: The no-orphan acceptance evidence is insufficient. Checking `tasklist /FI "PID eq <pid>"` against the stored pid proves little when `shell: true` may return a shell wrapper PID rather than the Vite/Node child. The AC should verify descendants and/or port 5173 is free, not just one PID.
findings.suggestedFix: Strengthen verification L to: (a) capture the dev-server pid AND the port-5173 listener pid (via `netstat -ano | findstr :5173` on Windows / `lsof -i :5173` on POSIX) before sending SIGTERM; (b) after MCP exits, assert BOTH pids are gone AND port 5173 is no longer listening; (c) additionally `wmic process where 'name="node.exe" or name="pnpm.cmd"' get processid` and assert none of the listed pids matches the pre-SIGTERM snapshot.
findings.resolution: Strengthened shutdown acceptance and Verification L to capture descendant and port-5173 listener PIDs, assert captured PIDs are gone, and verify port 5173 is no longer listening after MCP shutdown.

findings.description: The plan prescribes a pseudocode `readLockStatus()` algorithm but does not enumerate the refactor burden inside `sync-lock.mjs`. Existing `isLiveProcess()` (line 127-139) and the inline `JSON.parse` block (around line 75-86) are private. Implementing the helper requires either extracting them as named/exported helpers or inlining their logic into a new exported `readLockStatus()`. The plan should make the refactor explicit so the implementer doesn't accidentally duplicate logic.
findings.suggestedFix: Update the 'To modify' bullet for `sync-lock.mjs` to enumerate the sub-tasks: (1) extract the inline JSON parse + validation as `parseLockMetadata(buffer): { pid, process, startedAt } | null`; (2) extract the existing PID check as `isLockHolderAlive(pid: number): boolean` (export it); (3) write `readLockStatus(lockPath, opts)` that composes the two helpers + an `fs.stat`. Add unit tests for each extracted helper in the same module's test file.
findings.resolution: Amended the plan to spell out the sync-lock refactor helpers, type declarations, and same-module unit tests needed for readLockStatus.

findings.description: Plan AC line for sync-ralph-state summary references 'a unit test under `scripts/__tests__/` if one exists, or by an integration assertion in `sync-watch-status.test.ts`'. The conditional location creates ambiguity. The canonical location for sync-related script tests is unclear. If `scripts/__tests__/` does not exist (it doesn't on main), the implementer must fall back to the integration test — but `sync-watch-status.test.ts` is about lock-file parsing, not about the sync script's output format.
findings.suggestedFix: Pick one canonical location and commit. Recommend: add `tools/overview-mcp/src/__tests__/sync-now.test.ts` that spawns the real sync script in a tmp repo (via the existing helpers) and asserts the stdout summary line is parseable. This tests both the script-side emission AND the MCP tool's parser in one shot. Remove the conditional `scripts/__tests__/` reference.
findings.resolution: Amended the plan to make tools/overview-mcp/src/__tests__/sync-now.test.ts the canonical integration test for the sync summary output and removed the ambiguous scripts/__tests__/sync-watch-status fallback.

findings.description: The plan's prose recommends serial execution citing heavy merge churn, then offers a parallel handoff command using a JSON sidecar. This is internally inconsistent — the parallel path will be ineffective for cluster mcp-ops-tools (4 stories editing the same 5 files). An implementer reading just the handoff line could accidentally launch parallel execution against a serial-required cluster.
findings.suggestedFix: Tighten the prose under 'Suggested Decomposition': explicitly state that `execution_mode: serial` is REQUIRED for cluster mcp-ops-tools and the parallel handoff command is offered ONLY for completeness; recommend the serial handoff first. Alternatively, omit the parallel handoff command entirely and only show the serial one — the decomposition.json sidecar already records the serial requirement for any downstream tool that consumes it.
findings.resolution: Made serial execution explicitly required for mcp-ops-tools and replaced the parallel handoff command with the serial handoff command.

findings.description: US-004 is described as updating `stdio-tools-list.test.ts` to count 14 tools as an interim assertion, with the final count becoming 17 only after US-005/US-006 land. If those stories are merged or tests run between stories, the count drift will cause CI failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Update the smoke test count in each story as new tools are registered. Story US-004 → 14, US-005 → 15, US-006 → 17, US-007 confirms 17. Each story's PR should leave the test green. Add this to the per-story acceptance criteria in stories-outline.md.

findings.description: The existing `stdio-tools-list.test.ts` spawns the BUILT `tools/overview-mcp/dist/index.js`, not the TypeScript source. After source changes, a stale `dist/` would still report 10 tools. The plan does not call out the build prerequisite for running this smoke test.
findings.suggestedFix: Add to AC and to the test file: 'Run `pnpm --filter @codexu/overview-mcp build` before invoking `stdio-tools-list.test.ts`, or add a `pretest` hook that does so.' Verify vitest config or scripts to ensure the build runs as part of `pnpm test` invocation.

findings.description: Separating transient (build, sync-now) and long-lived (dev-server) into different code paths (module-level `isBuilding` flag for build; ad-hoc ring buffer inside each tool) duplicates the hardest parts of ProcessManager (line buffering, ring buffer, lifecycle) and misses the shutdown-cleanup benefit (see F-004).
findings.suggestedFix: Unify under ProcessManager: support spawning transient processes by reserved single-flight name ('build', 'sync-now') with an `oneShot: true` flag. ProcessManager.spawn returns AlreadyRunning if the name is taken (replaces the isBuilding boolean). On `'exit'`, oneShot entries are auto-removed from the Map (but stay alive in any `stopAll()` iteration that started before the exit). This eliminates the separate code paths and ensures stopAll catches in-flight transients.

findings.description: The shutdown integration test that starts the real Vite server through `dist/index.js` is heavyweight: it depends on Vite startup, port 5173 availability, and watcher startup. It will likely be flaky in CI and slow locally.
findings.suggestedFix: Split into two tests: (1) a unit test for `ProcessManager.stopAll()` using `node -e 'setInterval(...)'` children only — covers the manager contract; (2) a SKIP-by-default-on-CI integration test that uses real Vite, runnable manually on Windows. Mark the heavy test with `it.skipIf(process.env.CI)` or `describe.skipIf(!process.env.OVERVIEW_MCP_REAL_VITE)`.

findings.description: `dev_server.logs` says `tail` is both 'validated 1..1000' and 'clamped 1..1000'. Validation rejects invalid input; clamping coerces it. The plan needs to pick one to make the contract testable.
findings.suggestedFix: Pick `clamp`: zod schema declares `tail: z.number().int().optional().default(100)`; the tool implementation clamps via `Math.max(1, Math.min(1000, input.tail ?? 100))`. Update AC to: 'tail: out-of-range values are clamped to [1, 1000]; the tool never rejects on tail.' Update tests to assert clamping (tail=0 → 1 line, tail=99999 → 1000 lines).

findings.description: The plan says `sync.now` has no in-process lock because the OS lock will serialize. ACs do not define what concurrent `sync.now` calls return when the lock is held by the Vite-plugin watcher or another caller. Without a defined error, callers can't write reliable code.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an AC: 'If `sync.now` is called while `config.lockFile` is held by another holder (vite-plugin / standalone / another sync-now), the underlying script exits non-zero with a stderr line about lock contention. The MCP tool returns `{ ok: false, error: \'sync lock held by <process>\', lockHolderProcess: <label>, lockHolderPid: <pid> }` after parsing the lock metadata via `readLockStatus`.' Add a unit test covering this.

findings.description: AC for the stdio smoke test says 'the 7 new tool names appear in the listed-tools output' but does not require the test to assert the exact set. A drift that adds an 18th tool or renames one would be silently accepted by a count-only assertion.
findings.suggestedFix: Strengthen the AC: 'The test must assert (a) exact tool count of 17 AND (b) the exact set of names. Use `expect(toolNames).toEqual(new Set([...10 from Plan 09, ...7 from Plan 11]))` so any rename or addition forces an explicit test update.'
